title: Resume Mag'har face asset fix
final_messages: All touchups are installed and passed your live checks: chat, Skyborn’s first login, race names and portraits, tooltip text/placement, and single-line character names. Verified rollback backups are saved.

The new portraits and seven-column faction layout are installed. Please launch WoW fresh, check both genders’ Mag’har and Alliance/Horde Skyborne portraits, and send a screenshot of the race-selection screen so I can verify spacing, faction headings, and selection highlights.
The follow-up is installed. Please reopen WoW: are both name fields hidden on race selection, does the button now say “Customize,” and do First Name and Last Name both appear after clicking it?

Installed and visually confirmed: all six bordered portraits, the compact faction rows, and the corrected “Customize” label. Both name fields now appear only after opening customization.

Verified backups are saved for rollback.

The native Skyborne expansion is installed and worldserver is ready. Please launch WoW fresh and check both Skyborne genders in character creation: do the bodies render, do you see the extra controls (eyes, eyebrows, feathers, feather color, facial hair and ears), and do they change independently? Leave the client open; send a screenshot if anything looks wrong.

The control routing correction is installed. Please reopen WoW and leave either Skyborne gender visible in character creation, then tell me it’s ready. Check whether Hair Style now changes the style; I’ll read the live visibility and index buffers while the body is on screen.

The geometry repair is installed and worldserver is ready. Please launch WoW fresh and check male and female Skyborne: are their full bodies/faces visible, and do Hair Style, Hair Color, Eyebrows, Feathers, Facial Hair and Ears change the correct features? Please leave the client open on a Skyborne so I can verify the restored meshes.
The hairstyle-specific feather repair and rotation-control move are staged and checked. Please close WoW and Eclipse so I can replace the helper and archives, then tell me they’re closed.

The feather mapping fix and rotation-control move are installed; worldserver is ready. Please launch WoW fresh and test feathers while cycling hairstyles and feather colors for both genders. Do they now follow the hairstyle without overlapping, and are all four rotation controls below the first/last name fields? Keep a feathered Skyborne visible for verification.

Installed and visually confirmed: expanded Skyborne controls, hairstyle-matched feathers, and rotation controls below the name fields. Customization runs independently of WXL.

[Rebuild and rollback guide](/R:/Users/Zach/Documents/GitHub/EsteriaWoW/client-customization/README.md). Login/relog testing remains; face morphs and tattoos are still unimplemented.

Understood. **Customization will be implemented through a permanent `Wow.exe` patch and matching AzerothCore support**, independent of WXL APIs.

WXL can continue providing 64-race support and your other client features. The customization work will cover the extra creator controls, rendering, saved appearance data, Character Select, barber, and relog.

We’ll retain your **blue/purple Skyborne skins and no-horns preference**. No code changes yet.

Yes. We can make the customization expansion a **permanent `Wow.exe` patch**, with no WXL dependency.

For full independent controls, we would still need:

- Native rendering support for the extra geometry, materials, and face shapes.
- New character-creation controls.
- Client/server handling and storage for the additional appearance choices.
- Support in Character Select, in-game rendering, barber, and relog.

Skyborne currently also uses WXL’s **64-race extension**. Removing WXL entirely means moving that race support into the executable too.

Do you want **the customization expansion independent of WXL**, or **the entire Esteria client to run without WXL**?

**Yes—we can extend 3.3.5’s customization system and add controls to character creation.** The work has two parts:

- **More choices in the existing controls:** Most Skyborne skin, face, and hair counts fit within Wrath’s existing five appearance bytes. Restoring them primarily requires complete model, texture, geoset, and face-shape support. Our curated version removed options to get an initial working model.
- **Additional independent controls:** Eye color, eyebrow style, feather style/color, ears, and tattoos need extra saved appearance data. That requires client UI/runtime changes, server communication, and persistent character storage. Character Select, in-game rendering, barber changes, and relog must all use that data.

The current large-index/geoset visibility limitation also needs a proper runtime fix so we can retain the full geometry without pruning hairstyles.

I recommend doing this through the **existing WarcraftXL extension**, applying the client changes in memory while preserving `Wow.exe` on disk. A permanent executable patch is possible, but it would still need the same server and persistence work.

We can keep your **blue/purple palette and no-horns preference** while expanding everything else. No code changes yet.

For Skyborne’s first playable version, which customization scope do you prefer? Full face-shape support needs bone conversion and additional runtime work; a curated version can use the existing Wrath controls sooner.
- Curated presets first; expand after visual testing
- All 20 face shapes per gender from the start

Skyborne is installed and worldserver is ready. Please launch WoW fresh and test High Order or Windshaper Skyborne: both genders, Skin Color, Face, Hair, and Features. Do both models render correctly? Send screenshots if anything looks wrong.

The visibility repair is installed. Please launch WoW fresh and check both Skyborne genders again. Are the full bodies and faces visible now? Keep the client open so I can verify the selected geosets.

The current curated set includes normal Blood Elf colors and optional Demon Hunter horns from the Skyborne source. It also omitted female blue skins because those choices lacked matching face overlays. Should I make the first version focus on Skyborne’s blue/purple skins and feathers, or retain the broader source options too?
- Skyborne blue/purple skins and feathers; exclude horns
- Keep broader source skins and optional horns

Curated Skyborne is installed: **High Order 52 / Windshaper 53**.

Both genders are confirmed visible, with five blue/purple skins and working eyebrow/feather presets. Horns are excluded; all six checks pass.

Next: create a character and test login, movement, armor, Character Select, and relog. In-game acceptance remains unverified.

Skyborne’s main assets are present: **both base models, four collection models, 106 animations, and 1,101 textures**. What remains falls into three groups.

**1. Twelve missing texture paths referenced by the models**

These are absent from the converted pack:

| Model | Missing textures |
|---|---|
| Male body `7478487` | `7478487_7479201.blp`, `7478487_7479202.blp`, `eyes_lense.blp` |
| Female body `7478494` | `7478494_7479318.blp`, `7478494_7479319.blp`, `eyes_lense.blp` |
| Male Demon Hunter collection | `bloodelfmaledemonhorn.blp`, `bloodelfmale_dh_blindfolds.blp`, `bloodelfdemontabard.blp` |
| Female Demon Hunter collection | `bloodelf_female_dh_belt.blp`, `bloodelffemale_dh_horns.blp`, `bloodelf_female_dh_blindfolds.blp` |

The conversion planner omitted these dependencies. That explains why its report says **zero failed/skipped** despite the missing references. We need to extract them from the Forever source or provide verified replacements. Their availability in the original CASC source is still untested.

**2. Customization that hasn’t been translated**

- **20 Face choices per gender** depend on `.bone` shape overrides. Those 40 overrides were deliberately excluded because Wrath cannot consume them directly. Downloading them alone won’t enable those faces.
- Feathers, eyebrows, horns, and blindfolds use separate collection models. Their geometry needs merging, bone mapping, and compatible geoset selection.
- Tattoos, eye options, feathers, and accessories need mapping into Wrath’s five saved appearance fields.
- Body/face textures need compositor-compatible baking, including indexed textures and proper alpha overlays.

The collection geometry fits comfortably: approximately **47,836 male / 41,695 female vertices** if all three corresponding models are combined.

**3. Esteria integration**

The Skyborne manifest, detailed DBC allocations, appearance rows, character-screen entries, starting data, languages, and racials haven’t been implemented. **Race IDs 52/53 are already reserved**, and the shared race foundation exists.

The first concrete step should be recovering those twelve texture references and proving complete model dependencies. Then we can build the playable models and settle how much of the 40 face-shape choices to support initially.

**I recommend Highmountain Tauren next**, using Esteria’s reserved **Race 46, Horde**.

It has the smallest pack—**279 files**—with both gender models and the distinctive antlers already in the base geometry. It also avoids the large separate cosmetic collections that complicate several other candidates.

| Race | What makes its integration harder |
|---|---|
| **Highmountain** | Antler bone/geoset mapping, texture baking, and missing eye assets. Best next candidate. |
| **Mechagnome** | Mechanical limbs and modifications need collection merging, presets, and careful glove/boot/pants handling. Combined geometry is within the Wrath vertex budget. |
| **Earthen** | Large cosmetic collections need pruning: the female collection alone has **60,596 vertices**. Nine customization textures were skipped. |
| **Skyborne** | Good Blood Elf geometry reuse potential and no skipped conversion inputs, but missing referenced textures and **40 unsupported face-shape overrides** remain. |
| **Haranir** | Most extensive geometry/customization work. Large collections, 25 skipped textures, and very little mesh overlap with the installed HD Night Elf. |

**Highmountain’s converted M2s need adaptation before deployment.** Their animation tables contain only 13–15 sequence rows and many invalid lookup references. The safest Mag’har-style approach is to use isolated models derived from the working HD Tauren foundation, transplant the Highmountain antlers, and bake its Retail appearance into the native compositor layout.

Its five male and four female Retail Face choices also depend on `.bone` overrides. Exact face-shape parity requires additional work; curated legacy presets are the simpler initial scope.

My first implementation gate would be **working antlers and normal animations on both genders**, followed by fur, face, body-paint, customization, and server integration.

This analysis was read-only.

Both genders are now confirmed working, including Skin Color and Face cycling.

Fixed the invalid facial-hair overlay and moved backup MPQs out of `Data`, where they were overriding the new textures. Backups are preserved; **11/11 checks pass**.

I corrected the confirmed UV-mapping error and installed the rebuilt pack. Both genders now use Retail faces baked through the Orc2 model’s UVs; the stock male diagnostic is removed.

**11/11 tests pass**, live archives and server DBCs match, and worldserver is ready.

Launch WoW fresh and check both faces, Skin Color, and Face cycling. Send new screenshots—the male neon-green failure still needs live confirmation.

[Backup and verification report](</G:/3.3.5a - Backups/retroported-races-maghar-20260930-071112/live-verification.json>)

The interrupted deployment is repaired. **The diagnostic is fully installed and worldserver is ready.**

- Female textures have the palette rollback restored.
- Male FaceLower uses stock Orc2; FaceUpper remains Mag’har.
- All archive and server DBC checks passed; **10/10 tests passed**.

Launch WoW fresh and test both genders’ Skin and Face selectors. For males, check whether facial detail renders or the **solid neon-green failure** remains—ordinary Orc green coloring is expected during this diagnostic.

Send screenshots of both faces. Visual behavior is still unverified.

[Backup and verification report](</G:/3.3.5a - Backups/retroported-races-maghar-recovery-20260930-063117/live-verification.json>)

Yes. I read the conversation and confirmed the matching local code. **DevSpace stopped with a diagnostic staged, but its installation unverified.**

The handoff was:

- **Geometry:** Mag’har Race 45 was returned to working Wrath HD Orc2 models after the converted Retail geometry caused mostly invisible bodies.
- **Customization:** Retail Mag’har appearance remains, with **9 skin colors and 9 independent faces** per gender. Your last test confirmed bodies and skin cycling worked again.
- **Male issue:** Faces remained green. A palette-byte experiment failed to fix this and broke female faces.
- **Latest staged change:** That palette experiment was reverted. **Only male FaceLower now points to stock Orc2 textures**; male FaceUpper and female faces retain Mag’har-derived textures.
- **Stopping point:** DevSpace reported **10/10 tests passing**, then timed out during installation and received 502 errors. It could not confirm the diagnostic reached the live client.

There is also an unresolved extraction assumption: the generator cuts the Retail 512×512 face material at `(0,320,256,64)` and `(0,384,256,128)`. Those coordinates were never proven correct and could explain the mismatched facial appearance.

I confirmed the diagnostic and rollback are present in [the pack generator](/R:/Users/Zach/Documents/GitHub/EsteriaWoW/tools/retroported_race_pack.py:404), with staging under `G:\RetroPorterWork\maghar\integration\latest`.

**The next step is to verify the live archives against that stage before another client test.** That test should help separate a generated FaceLower problem from a Race 45 lookup/compositor problem. I haven’t changed anything yet.

title: Port Highmountain Tauren race
final_messages: The repair is installed. Please launch WoW fresh, log into Highmountain, and leave the character visible for about 20 seconds before logging out. Tell me when it’s ready so I can verify that nearby NPC list links stay intact.

Fixed and live. The extra-appearance field registration was overwriting neighboring NPC memory; the repair removes that unsafe registration while preserving appearance updates.

Your logout/relog, ordinary-race logout, client exit, and Highmountain checks all passed without crashes or regressions. Race assets and catalogs remain unchanged, and verified backups are saved.

I recommend investigating **Highmountain’s native appearance-listener cleanup** before changing the working assets.

Both recent crashes stop at `0x0074604E` during unit destruction. WoW is unlinking an object-field notification list, but its previous-link pointer is null. The second dump confirms that malformed list state. This explains why gameplay works and logout/exit fails.

The leading suspect is an appearance listener that remains attached, gets detached twice, or is modified during teardown. The helper immediately reapplies geometry from its field-change callback, and its cached character pointers have no destruction cleanup. Those are concrete lifecycle weaknesses, although the dumps do **not** establish which operation corrupted the list.

My recommended approach:

1. **Identify the damaging write** with a debugger watchpoint on the affected list’s previous-link field (`unit + 0x4C`). This should precede another speculative patch.
2. Correct the responsible listener’s ownership and detach sequence. Prevent appearance refreshes once unit destruction begins; defer refreshes outside notification dispatch if reentrancy is responsible.
3. Clear `highmountainContext` and remove the character’s `highmountainExtra` entry when its appearance component is freed.
4. Verify repeated logout/login and client exits for both genders, plus an unrelated race.

I would **not recommend simply skipping the null write at the crash address**: that would leave corrupted notification state behind.

No files were changed.

Installed a new repair for both genders. It restores missing weapon sheath events and replaces corrupted animation, opacity, and camera data. Checks pass, backups are verified, and unrelated assets remain unchanged.

Please launch WoW fresh and test:

- Talking: stays visible.
- `/dance`: stays opaque without crashing.
- Unsheathing: sword and shield move into the hands.

These still need your live confirmation.

The Highmountain animation repair is installed. After a fresh launch, do both genders remain fully visible while talking and dancing, and do drawn weapons/shields move into the correct hands? Please also check jumping, attacks and casting; leave the client open on any failing animation or attachment.

Installed repairs for talk/dance visibility and weapon-socket animation data. Automated checks pass; face geometry and eyes are preserved.

Please launch fresh and test both genders’ chat, dancing, and weapon/shield drawing. Live confirmation is still needed.

Installed the eye-material repair for both genders. Checks pass, and the confirmed face geometry is unchanged.

Please launch fresh and test Eye Color and Eyesight on both genders.

Highmountain’s full customization needs native helper and worldserver changes beyond the previous five-byte codec. AGENTS.md forbids builds without an explicit request. Do you authorize building the native helper and worldserver for this port, then restarting only ac-worldserver after verified installation?

Highmountain Tauren is installed and worldserver is ready. After a fresh WoW launch, do both genders render correctly, do the 20 male/22 female controls change the intended features, and do creation, chat, animations, Character Select portraits/tooltips, and relog work? Please leave the client open on a Highmountain and send a screenshot or crash report if anything fails.

Highmountain Tauren is installed, and worldserver is ready.

- 20 male/22 female controls, all nine face shapes, and 349/341 animation sequences.
